A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of multidimensional language-model features. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original SAE experiments, feature-discovery analyses, weekday/month task accuracies, activation interventions, and regression analyses, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds empirical irreducibility measurements on GPT-2 features and experiments with time-qualified weekday representations.

M1.justification: The stated Section 4 recipe narrows clustering from cosine or Jaccard similarity to cosine similarity. This changes the proposed options, but Appendix F retains the same implemented spectral and graph clustering procedures. The SAE objective, circular probing/intervention procedure, and EVR method remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds synthetic inputs combining weekdays with very early/very late and morning/evening qualifiers, extending evaluation to contextual variation within a day. The training corpora, synthetic-circle datasets, and original weekday/month arithmetic tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the same models in Table 1 and retain the same intervention controls: no-op, whole-layer patching, top-five-PCA patching, and average ablation. The added analyses introduce no competing comparison method.

E3.justification: The new cluster analysis averages irreducibility scores over adjacent PCA planes 1-2 through 4-5. The continuity experiments project time-qualified inputs at Mistral layer 30 into a PCA basis obtained from weekday inputs. These are additional evaluation protocols; the existing arithmetic and intervention settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a substantive validation connecting the formal irreducibility tests to actual GPT-2 feature clusters, comparing identified circles with other clusters in Figures 2-3. Section 5.3 and Figure 19 additionally test whether weekday representations accommodate intermediate times. The earlier synthetic tests, off-distribution interventions, and EVR analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G.3 retains the same normal-approximation 96% confidence intervals over intervention outcomes. The 20-plus-20 prompt-pair patching design and synthetic SAE seed disclosures are also unchanged. No new uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds real-feature irreducibility results, including mixture index 0.4750 and separability index 0.9506 for the weekday projection in Figure 2, cluster-level comparisons in Figure 3, and time-dependent representation shifts in Figures 9 and 19. These extend the findings rather than improve retained benchmark scores: all four tables and the earlier intervention and EVR results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a claimed upper bound and proof to the previously lower-bound-only capacity theorem. Definitions 1-2 also remove the explicit sparsity parameter and restrict mixture weights to 0 < w < 1. The added upper-bound statement and the proof's final expression are inconsistent, so this is a substantive theoretical revision without a clearly established correctness improvement.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the novelty claim from the first emergent circular representation in a language model to the first causal circular representations of concepts. It explicitly challenges the one-dimensional part of the linear representation hypothesis and adds the claim that circular representations respect continuous time. The central discovery and causal-use claims remain.

C2.justification: V1 interprets its capacity construction as suggesting strong pressure toward compressed features; v2 acknowledges an exponential gap between bounds and makes that interpretation conditional on lower-bound tightness. V2 also interprets the new continuity results, explains how interference obscures output circles before EVR, and questions whether individual SAE features are suitable causal mediators.

D1.justification: V2 supplies concrete reproduction details for the added analyses: PCA-plane selection and score averaging, temporal prompt templates, the selected model layer, and the reference projection basis. Existing SAE hyperparameters, clustering settings, hardware, runtime information, and experiment-code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises its positioning by acknowledging Yedidia's earlier positional circles and distinguishing causal representations of latent concepts. It adds discussion of the linear/multidimensional distinction through Olah, Csordas, and Mendel, plus mediator and capacity references. The earlier nonlinear toy-model discussion citing Kim and Suzuki and Shai et al. is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, related work, clustering rationale, and regression narrative are substantially rewritten. Capacity theory moves out of the main text, detailed EVR exposition moves into Appendix J, and a continuity subsection is added. Citation style, terminology, headings, and author ordering also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 2-3 and 9/19, redraws the intervention schematic, relocates the synthetic irreducibility and Mistral EVR displays into appendices, and places the two patching figures together. Typography and spacing change throughout. The new continuity plots have inconsistent early/late versus morning/evening labels and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the connection between its definitions and real model features, adds useful continuity evidence, and more carefully scopes novelty and capacity interpretations. These improve a paper whose principal causal results were already present in v1. However, the new capacity theorem conflicts with its derivation, and the continuity figures have mismatched labels and captions. These problems temper the empirical and explanatory gains.
